reviewed_by: Claude Code, replacing the Butler deployment wind-down with Core project holds in the deployer
reason: Deployments that need a quiet boundary relied on asking Butler to pause work, which did not hold on 2026-11-20. The deployer now uses Core's project holds (#1232): at a host restart with workers older than #1023 it holds each busy project (and any that becomes busy), waits until no held project has chat work, restarts, and releases only the holds it placed, also when activation fails. New hold and release-holds commands place and release holds for a whole-Core stop or a project wind-down; every hold is saved in project-holds.json, separate from deployer-state.json, until Core confirms its release. A Core without the hold route (framework 404/405) falls back to the existing bounded wait. AGENTS.md now describes the hold procedure and keeps the Butler procedure only for Cores older than #1232. Selected: host restart suite (5 new hold cases), deploy resume, dead-owner activation and staged deployer suites.
exclusions: Deployer scripts, their README, tests and AGENTS.md only; no Core or UI change. tests/test_simulation_host_activation.py and tests/test_deployer_protocol.py pass locally except one onefile identity case that also fails on unmodified main here; two host-switch signalling cases in the host restart suite fail locally on unmodified main and pass in CI.
